subject: Renewal pricing — tiered commit restructure and bridge plan
messages:
From: Javier Campos <javier@orionsystems.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal conversation — usage bump and pricing questions

Connor,

Hope you're well. We're preparing our renewal for Q1 2027 and expect a sizable usage increase across our customer-facing features — roughly +60% token volume on average and an extra 3 dedicated concurrent sessions during peak. We'd like to understand options on pricing/commit structure and whether you can offer a temporary price hold while we ramp.

Specific asks from my side:
- Do you have a path to keep unit pricing flat for the first 3 months of expanded usage?
- Any intake credits or one-time credits to offset migration/ingestion costs?
- We're evaluating a larger commit but need a tiered structure so we don't overcommit if ramp is slower.

Can we schedule a short call? Procurement will likely join.

Thanks,
Javier
Director, Platform Engineering
Orion Systems
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Javier Campos <javier@orionsystems.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 09:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation — usage bump and pricing questions

Javier — thanks for the heads up and congrats on the growth. High level options based on what you described (we've also attached an initial draft amendment and a pricing spreadsheet):

1) Standard 12-month renewal (single commit)
   - 10% list discount on current unit price for a 12-month committed spend equal to your current run-rate * 12 + planned expansion delta
   - No separate credits; overages billed at committed unit rate + 20%

2) Tiered commit restructure (recommended for phased ramp)
   - Breakpoint tiers: 0–75% of commit (base rate), 75–125% (-12% unit price), >125% (-18% unit price)
   - Monthly true-ups to adjust tiered pricing; protects you from long-term overcommit while rewarding predictable increased volume

3) Bridge plan (short-term price hold)
   - 6-month price hold on current unit price for the incremental volume above your present baseline while you ramp to the higher commit level
   - To enable this we ask for a signed amendment and a short-term commit increase that phases in after month 6

Additional concession we can consider: a one-time expansion credit applied to the first invoice after signing (proposed: $25,000) — approvals required for non-standard credits.

Next steps I suggest: quick procurement call this week, then I will loop in Marissa and RevOps (Rishi) to finalize credit approvals and sign-off. If you can share desired contract dates (effective date + renewal term) and PO cadence, I can tailor the amendment.

Attachments: Orion_Renewal_Draft_v1.pdf, pricing_table_breakdown.xlsx

Best,
Connor O'Brien
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
connor.obrien@redwood.ai
From: Tina Park <tina.park@orionsystems.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 14:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation — usage bump and pricing questions

Connor / Marissa —

Thanks for the fast reply and the options. A few points from procurement:
- We need a longer price hold option if possible; our fiscal planning runs through March 2027 and any transient hits to unit pricing will be hard to absorb across FY lines. Can you extend the bridge plan to 9 months?
- The one-time credit is helpful; procurement prefers credits to be applied against overages (usage-based credits), not just first invoice, so it smooths the ramp risk.
- For the tiered commit, can you add a fourth breakpoint at >200% with an aggressive unit price? We expect certain feature launches could spike volume.

We can do a call Friday 11/6 at 11am PT if that works. Also tagging procurement email procurement@orionsystems.com for PO process details.

Regards,
Tina Park
Sr. Procurement Manager
Orion Systems
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Tina Park <tina.park@orionsystems.com>, Javier Campos <javier@orionsystems.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal pricing — proposed compromise and next steps

Tina / Javier — appreciate the clarity. After internal review here's a pragmatic compromise that we can present to your finance team: 

- Bridge plan: extend to 9 months (meets procurement ask) with current unit price held for incremental volume above baseline during that window. After month 9, tiered commit pricing phases in.
- Tiered commit adjustments: add 4th breakpoint (>200%) with an additional -22% unit price at that top tier.
- Credit structure: we can convert the one-time $25,000 to a usage credit pool that rolls across the first 6 invoice cycles, applied to overages and excess usage.

This exception requires executive/RevOps sign-off for the extended hold + convertible credit. Requesting approval from Marissa and Rishi for the credit structure and 9-month hold. If approved, Legal will accept a short amendment and we'll push DocuSign.

I propose the following immediate next steps:
1) Internal approvals (Marissa / Rishi) — this week
2) Procurement signs amendment via DocuSign (we'll supply prepared amendment) — target 11/18
3) PO issued to Redwood and billing kickoff on effective date

I've attached updated license_amendment_tiered_v2.docx for you to review.

Thanks,
Connor
